paper.title: Direct observation of quantum scattering oscillations in the controlled Kr* + Rb cold collision

research.objective: Observe quantum scattering oscillations in cold ionizing collisions between metastable krypton (Kr*) and rubidium (Rb) atoms by combining laser cooling with velocity-mapped ion imaging (VMI) to control collision energy from 15 mK to 8 K and measure differential cross sections (DCS).
research.system: Kr* (4p^5 5s[3/2]_2, 9.9 eV) + Rb (5S_{1/2}, F=2) cold collisions leading to Penning ionization (PI) and associative ionization (AI).
key_findings: Pronounced quantum interference between partial waves emerges below 1 K as de Broglie wavelength approaches interaction range.
Angular oscillation period scales as θ_p ∝ E^{-1/3}, consistent with Langevin capture model for van der Waals-dominated collisions.
Interference patterns in angular distribution–collision temperature (A-T) spectrum are highly sensitive to long-range potential shape and reveal subtle shape resonances.
Backward scattering enhanced at specific collision energies (~40, 70, 120, 170 mK) due to shape resonances in specific partial waves (e.g., l=11 at 32 mK).
Radial oscillations in Rb+ kinetic energy distribution originate from Fourier transform of √Γ ψ* (autoionization transition matrix element).
Experimental results corroborated by theoretical calculations, but discrepancies highlight need for multichannel models and accurate ab initio ionization widths.
methods: Laser cooling and trapping of Kr* and Rb in two vertically separated MOTs (60 cm apart).
Moving molasses technique to launch Kr* atoms with controlled velocity toward Rb MOT.
Velocity map imaging (VMI) detection of ion products (Rb+ from PI, KrRb+ from AI).
Inverse Abel transformation to obtain DCS.
Time-independent quantum scattering calculations on computed potential energy curves (RASSCF with spin-orbit coupling for V*, analytical for V+).
Phenomenological exponential fit for imaginary part of V* (autoionization width).
Energy-dependent convolution to account for experimental energy spread.

states.intermediate_complex: (KrRb)* transient complex on lowest electronically excited adiabatic PEC

electronic_structure.states_calculated: lowest electronically excited adiabatic PEC for Kr*+Rb

scattering.method: time-independent quantum method for scattering wave functions on V* and V+ surfaces under s-wave electron approximation
scattering.autoionization_treatment: phenomenological exponential fit for Γ(R), s-wave electron approximation
scattering.energy_convolution: energy-dependent convolution applied to ion energy distribution to account for experimental spread

langevin_model.validity: for long-range C6/R^6 potential, nonresonant cases

theory.autoionization_matrix_element: Fourier transform of √Γ ψ* from coordinate to momentum space, modulated by fast-oscillating cosine term

numerical.vmi_resolution: insufficient to analyze KrRb+ ions with ~5 m/s velocity
numerical.partial_waves_calculated: up to l_max determined by centrifugal barrier
numerical.potential_modifications: two modified long-range potentials (35-45 bohr) tested for sensitivity analysis

differential_cross_section.units: arbitrary units (normalized to total VMI intensity)

kinetic_energy_distribution_Rb+.features: oscillatory structure, nearly independent of collision energy

total_cross_section.note: experiment lacks resonant features predicted by theory

A_T_spectrum.sensitivity: highly sensitive to long-range potential (35-45 bohr)

results.quantum_regime: below 200 mK, pronounced oscillatory structures in DCS (angular and radial)
results.classical_regime: above 200 mK, oscillations blurred by many partial waves and VMI resolution
results.angular_scaling: θ_p ∝ E^{-1/3} from 15 mK to 1 K, consistent with Langevin model for van der Waals collisions
results.shape_resonances: observed as enhanced backward scattering at specific energies; theory predicts resonances in specific partial waves (e.g., l=11 at 32 mK)
results.radial_oscillations: originate from Fourier transform of √Γ ψ*; cutoff at 0.16 eV determined by V* well depth
results.theory_experiment_agreement: qualitative agreement for angular oscillations and energy distributions; discrepancies in resonance positions/amplitudes and fine structure
results.potential_sensitivity: A-T spectrum highly sensitive to long-range potential shape (35-45 bohr)

Fig.1.description: Experimental setup, energy levels, and potential energy curves. (A) Two MOTs with moving molasses launching Kr* toward Rb MOT, VMI detection. (B) Energy levels of Kr and Rb, schematic of autoionizing (KrRb)* complex. (C) PECs V* (metastable) and V+ (ionic), imaginary part Γ, and V*-V+ difference indicating electron kinetic energy.

Fig.2.description: VMI data at 40, 200, and 5100 mK. (A,E,I) Experimental DCS via inverse Abel transform. (B,F,J) Theoretical velocity distribution. (C,G,K) Angular distributions with θ_p marked. (D,H,L) Kinetic energy distributions of Rb+ ions.

Fig.3.description: Angular distribution analysis. (A) Experimental A-T spectrum (angular DCS vs collision energy). (B) Theoretical A-T spectrum with -1/3 power-law lines and resonance arrows. (C) Angular period vs collision energy showing -1/3 scaling. (D) Partial wave contributions at various energies, showing resonance enhancement at l=11 for 32 mK.

Fig.4.description: Sensitivity of A-T spectrum to Kr*+Rb PEC. (A) Ab initio PEC and two modified potentials. (B) Angular DCS from ab initio (top) and modified potentials (middle, bottom). Modified potential 1 matches experiment better.

Fig.5.description: Energy distribution of Rb+ ions. (A) Normalized experimental kinetic energy distributions at different collision energies. (B) Theoretical kinetic energy distributions. (C) Normalized momentum distribution of √Γ ψ* showing similar spectral profiles.

equations.autoionization_matrix_element: Fourier transform of √Γ ψ* from coordinate to momentum space, modulated by fast-oscillating cosine term

experimental: VMI resolution insufficient to analyze low-velocity KrRb+ ions (~5 m/s) from AI.
Energy spread: 20% at 15 mK, 1% at 8 K.
Angular resolution limited, blurs oscillations above 200 mK.
Total cross section measured but lacks resonant features.
theoretical: Single-channel model (lowest spin-orbit-coupled adiabatic PEC only) ignores multichannel effects (electron spins, spin-dependent interactions).
Phenomenological exponential fit for autoionization width Γ(R) rather than ab initio.
Limited accuracy in long-range van der Waals potential shape.
Discrepancies in resonance positions and amplitudes between theory and experiment.
general: Need for accurate ab initio ionization widths.
Benchmark cold collision experiments needed to validate theory.
